claims.text: As a traditional sushi and seafood-bowl counter, soy sauce is used throughout for sushi and donburi; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat. No gluten-free soy sauce or wheat-free preparation is documented.
The kitchen is entirely seafood-focused, with all dishes built around fish, shellfish, uni and roe, so cross-contact with animal products is unavoidable.
Edomae sushi is built on vinegared rice, soy-based nikiri/tsume sauces, and soy sauce, so gluten is pervasive throughout the meal; no gluten-free handling is documented.
Standard Japanese soy sauce (wheat-containing) and brushed nikiri/tsume sauces are integral to the sushi served here.
The entire omakase is seafood-based with fish-derived dashi (freshly shaved katsuobushi at the counter); there are no vegan dishes.

name: 鮨 歴々 近江町店 (Sushi Rekireki Omicho-ten)

claims.text: Edomae sushi counter using wheat-based soy sauce and seasoned vinegar rice; no gluten-free handling or dedicated equipment is documented, so cross-contact with wheat is expected.
Standard nigiri preparation relies on soy sauce, which is typically wheat-based; no wheat-free soy sauce is mentioned.
The entire menu is fish- and seafood-based with fish dashi; no vegan options are offered, so vegan cross-contact is unavoidable.

name: 大衆酒場 魚八 はなれ (Taishu Sakaba Uohachi Hanare)

claims.text: Menu includes fried items (fries, tempura-style dishes) and is a general izakaya kitchen; no dedicated gluten-free preparation is documented, so cross-contact with wheat is likely.
Sushi, sashimi and oden are served/seasoned with standard Japanese soy sauce and dashi, which contain wheat; no wheat-free soy sauce is mentioned.
Oden and dishes use fish/kombu dashi and the kitchen centers on seafood; no vegan preparation is documented.

name: 手打そば 更科藤井 (Teuchi Soba Sarashina Fujii)

claims.text: The kitchen hand-cuts wheat-bound nihachi soba (80% buckwheat / 20% wheat) as its standard, so any 100% buckwheat (juwari) option is made in the same wheat-handling environment - cross-contamination is essentially unavoidable.
Soba tsuyu and the small side dishes rely on standard Japanese soy sauce, which contains wheat; no wheat-free seasoning is documented.
The dipping broth is built on bonito (katsuo) dashi and the menu centers on duck and seafood, so plant-only diners cannot assume the noodles, broth, or shared kitchen are animal-free.

name: 特別名勝兼六園 堤亭 (Tokubetsu Meishō Kenrokuen Tsutsumitei)

claims.text: Jibu-ni is traditionally thickened with wheat flour and seasoned with wheat-based soy sauce, and the menu prominently features udon and soba; assume wheat is present throughout the savory offerings.
The kitchen centers on duck/meat jibu-ni and seafood (sweet-shrimp bowl); dashi and broths likely contain animal products, so even vegetable or sweet items may share preparation surfaces.
As a 甘味処, matcha tea, plum juice, and rice-based sweets (dango, ankoro-mochi) are available, giving non-meat diners some options alongside the savory Kaga dishes.

Traditional Kaga kaiseki built on wheat-based soy sauce and bonito/kombu dashi; signature jibu-ni traditionally uses flour-dusted protein, so gluten is intrinsic to the cuisine. No gluten-free preparation is documented.
Kaga cuisine here relies on standard Japanese soy sauce and dashi-based seasonings, which contain wheat; no wheat-free soy alternative is mentioned.
Menus center on seafood (crab porridge, sea bream, sashimi) and dashi; no vegan or vegetarian course is documented, so animal-derived stock and seafood are pervasive.
Fully reservation-based with bespoke multi-course service, so dietary requests can in principle be raised when booking well in advance, though no specific accommodation is documented.
All cooking happens on one shared central iron griddle where pork belly, yakisoba and other dishes are prepared together, so cross-contact with wheat is unavoidable.

The defining secret tare is made with three kinds of miso plus many other ingredients and is used on the signature dishes; standard Japanese miso and the accompanying soy-based seasonings contain wheat, so the sauce is not gluten-free.
Every main is meat-based (grilled pork belly, tonkatsu, pork soup) and cooked on the shared pork-fat griddle, so even side items cannot be considered free of animal cross-contact.
